## Natural history notes

A medium-sized predatory stink bug characterized by its shield-shaped body, bold black-and-orange to black-and-red patterning, and anchor-like dark marking across the back. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, roadsides, and other open or semi-open habitats where caterpillars and other soft-bodied insects are common. Unlike many plant-feeding stink bugs, it is mainly predatory, using its piercing beak to feed on caterpillars, beetle larvae, and other insects, making it a beneficial natural enemy in native plant communities and gardens.
